flags: minor: partial-fraction decomposition is at the edge of SAT scope, but substituting x=1 and x=-2 makes it solvable with routine steps

Q061-02.notes: Multiply by the conjugate: x(sqrt(x+9)+3)/x = sqrt(x+9)+3. Choice C is the error of writing (x+9)-9 as x+6 or similar. Desmos check works too.

Q061-03.notes: Zeros of x^2-9 are ±3. Case 1: the quadratic has a double root, k^2=16, k=±4 (root ∓2, not ±3), so 3 zeros. Case 2: the quadratic shares a root with ±3: the product of roots is 4, so the roots are 3 and 4/3 (k=-13/3) or -3 and -4/3 (k=13/3). Positive k: 4+13/3=25/3 (8.333). Students who find only k=4 enter 4.

Q061-04.notes: Vertex (5,k-25); roots 5±h with h^2=25-k; the depth equals h^2, and for an equilateral triangle depth = sqrt(3)h, so h=sqrt(3), 25-k=3, k=22.

Q061-05.notes: x^2-8x=16 gives two roots summing to 8; x^2-8x=-16 gives a double root x=4; sum of distinct solutions 12. Traps: 8 (one case only) or 16 (counting 4 twice).

Q061-06.notes: Intersections at x=4 (y=19) and x=-2 (y=-5); slope 24/6=4. Adding the equations gives 2y=8x+6, y=4x+3. Desmos makes it easy.

Q061-07.notes: (x+2)^2-9 = x^2+4x-5 = (x-1)(x+5). B also gives -5 at x=0, so a single test value at x=0 does not eliminate it.

Q061-11.notes: b^2=0.75, f(5)/f(1)=b^4=0.5625, so 43.75% less. Traps: 50% (linear doubling) and 56.25% (ratio instead of decrease).

Q061-14.notes: Center (5,-3); tangent to the x-axis means r=3; r^2=34-c=9 gives c=25.

Q061-16.notes: Angle DAG = 360-90-108 = 162; AD=AG, so the base angles are (180-162)/2 = 9. The figure-free description is unambiguous.

Q061-17.notes: Coordinates: P=(10/3,4) (AP:PE=2:1 from similar triangles). Shoelace on B(10,0),C(10,6),E(5,6),P(10/3,4) gives 25. Equivalently, triangle BCD (30) minus triangle DEP (0.5*5*2=5).

Q061-18.notes: Kite symmetry: angle B = angle D = (360-120)/2 = 120.

Q061-19.notes: 216-2(4π)+2π(2)(6)=216+16π. D forgets to remove the two circles; A ignores the inside of the hole.

Q061-20.notes: Horizontal offsets 6 (45°) and 6/sqrt3=2sqrt3 (60°); AB=16+2sqrt3; area = 3(26+2sqrt3) = 78+6sqrt3. D omits the 1/2; C uses 6sqrt3 as the offset.

Q061-21.notes: Water surface radius = 6*6/9 = 4; volume = (1/3)π(16)(6) = 32π; depth = 32π/36π = 8/9 (0.8888 or .8889). Trap: using radius 6 gives 2.

Q061-23.notes: 0.65p-40 >= 250 gives p >= 446.15, so 447. Traps: 446 (rounding down) or 0.35-based setup.

Q061-24.notes: Rear gear at 80*48/16 = 240 rpm; 240*2.1 = 504 m/min = 30.24 km/h. Fits the 5-character entry limit. Values are realistic.

Q061-25.notes: Cement = 4.5/6 = 0.75 m^3; 0.75/0.035 = 21.43, so 22 bags. A rounds down; C uses 1/3 of the mix; D uses the whole 4.5 m^3.

Q061-26.notes: 17% response rate, so nonresponse bias; random selection does not fix self-selected returns.
